# Cara (01, architect) — BAD-015

## Brief
Objective: close out phase 3 of the profiles design with evidence, then reconcile the two competing hosting approaches for `my.badtakes.io/@handle` into one dated design spec that an engineer can build from without asking questions. You write the spec only; you build nothing.

Context. Ticket BAD-015 (project BadTakes) is phase 4 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-20-user-profiles-and-handles-design.md: public profile pages, then the handle on export end cards. Phases 1-2 shipped 2026-08-21. Phase 3 (admin moderation) appears built. Phase 4 is not: firebase.json has no `/@` route, and the app already prints `my.badtakes.io/@handle` (src/handles.js PROFILE_HOST, renderer/app.js:1039, web/account.js:338) as a URL that resolves to nothing. The 2026-08-20 design chose a second Firebase App Hosting backend `profiles/` with SSR and 60-second ISR. The later docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-public-scene-pages-design.md chose prerendered static pages on the same host for scene pages, but that design was never built (scripts/build-web.js has no prerender step, no publicEntry, no sitemap). Another member is building the end-card half in parallel from the 2026-08-20 design (section "The handle on exports"); do not redesign it.

Part 1, phase 3 close-out (a short section of the spec). Confirm with file:line evidence that admin release pairs with a reserved_handles entry as the design requires: admin/src/lib/actions.ts releaseHandle (around line 1065) calls private.release_handle(email, reserve, note) in one transaction; check that the SQL function in server/supabase/migrations/0019_profile_moderation.sql inserts the reservation when reserve is true, and whether the checkbox in admin/src/components/ProfileControls.tsx defaults to on (the design says release "should almost always be paired"). Compare the built screens against the design's moderation table (rail entry, /profiles list, ?tab=profile, the reserved list at /accounts/handles/reserved rather than /profiles/reserved) and the AuditAction members. State "phase 3 is complete" or list each gap precisely. Build nothing for it; gaps are proposals (`spud proposal file`) unless they block phase 4.

Part 2, the hosting decision. Decide how `my.badtakes.io/@handle` is served, with reasons, and record the losing options and why they lost. Weigh at least:
 (a) the designed second App Hosting backend `profiles/` (the admin/ shape: admin/apphosting.yaml, admin/README.md). Account for the fact that my.badtakes.io is today the Firebase Hosting `my` target serving the static dist/web SPA (firebase.json, .github/workflows/deploy-web.yml, scripts/build-web.js, scripts/ensure-web-hosting.js): an App Hosting backend takes its own domain and Hosting cannot rewrite to one, so say what happens to the SPA and the domain.
 (b) a Firebase Hosting rewrite of `/@**` on the `my` target to a Cloud Run service: either a small new service, or a route on the existing render service that .github/workflows/deploy-render.yml already builds from the root Dockerfile (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-10-web-render-service-design.md, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-10-render-service-handoff.md, scripts/web-api.js). Check that Hosting-to-Cloud-Run rewrites are documented and what they require (same project, region, invoker permission).
 (c) a Hosting rewrite to a 2nd-gen Cloud Function.
 (d) prerender at build time, the 2026-09-09 choice: show why it does or does not fit a database-backed page (a handle claimed after the last deploy must resolve; the design says "the URL always resolves"; a suspension must 404 without a redeploy).
 (e) a static shell at `/@*` that fetches a public read endpoint client-side: say what that does to OG unfurling, which is the design's stated reason for SSR.
The decision must address each of these explicitly: correct per-handle OG tags; my.badtakes.io is Cloudflare-proxied with a long edge cache (read /Users/ericlugo/.claude/projects/-Users-ericlugo-Personal-BadTakes/memory/my-badtakes-is-cloudflare-proxied.md): which Cache-Control the page must emit, what the edge will do with it, and how long a suspension takes to become a 404 for a visitor (the design accepts a minute; say what this choice gives and whether a purge is ever needed); suspended profiles 404, never a tombstone; normalization redirects (/@Eric, /eric, /@eric/ to /@eric); robots and sitemap posture; the read path connects as the `profiles_reader` role from server/supabase/migrations/0012_profiles.sql (lines 184-191: nologin, column-level select without email), so say exactly how a service authenticates as it (a login role that inherits it, `set role`, a pooler user, or a dedicated function), where that credential lives (a CI secret and a runtime secret; never a legacy JWT key, see .claude/skills/server-changes/SKILL.md), and how the required runtime test "select email as profiles_reader is refused" is exercised in this phase (the design says phase 4 owns it); nothing under web/ that ships into mobile/www may change behaviour there (scripts/build-mobile.js calls the same buildWeb); the gate, the CSP and showView in web/app.js stay untouched (the 2026-09-09 design's reasons); how the thing deploys (backend changes deploy from CI only, see .claude/skills/server-changes/SKILL.md and server/README.md; name the workflow and what it needs); how it is verified locally and in CI (which tier of .claude/skills/implementing-changes/SKILL.md proves each part; a migration needs the Server integration check); cost and cold starts if a new service is involved.

Part 3, the implementation plan for the next engineer: the ordered file list with what each file does, the next migration number if one is needed (`ls server/supabase/migrations/` first; never edit an applied one), the exact firebase.json and workflow changes, the tests to write and the commands that prove them, and a named list of every secret, DNS record, IAM grant or console step that only Eric can do, so Spud can ask him in one go. Add a short section "What this changes for the end-card member": normally nothing; if the URL shape or host differs from src/handles.js profileUrl, say so.

Read first: the two designs named above; docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-23-my-badtakes-io-web-app-design.md; docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-01-badtakes-on-the-web-design.md; web/CLAUDE.md; server/CLAUDE.md; admin/CLAUDE.md; server/README.md; CLAUDE.md at the repo root; firebase.json; the three workflows deploy-web.yml, deploy-render.yml, server-deploy.yml; migrations 0012, 0019, 0027; scripts/build-web.js; scripts/ensure-web-hosting.js; admin/apphosting.yaml; the Firebase docs for Hosting rewrites to Cloud Run and for App Hosting custom domains (WebFetch is available; cite what you relied on).

House style for the spec: match the existing specs in docs/superpowers/specs/ (a dated title, "What this is", "Approaches considered" with the losers and why, numbered sections, "Testing", "Not in scope", "Assumptions to push back on"). State decisions, not options. Under 400 lines.
